first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A company called Wedded Concierge plans weddings in Portugal for couples from the US, UK and Australia, with one advisor looking after you. The top is mostly about Sintra palaces, Algarve cliffs and the legal paperwork. I get that they plan weddings. I can't tell yet whether they're a full service destination wedding planner or a booking desk that passes you to venues.

attention_map.quote: Wedded Concierge plans weddings in Portugal for couples from Australia, the United States and the United Kingdom, with one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend.
attention_map.why: Good. It names the US and UK, so I'm not reading something written only for Australians. 'One Wedded Advisor' is the right promise, but I don't know who that person is or how senior they are.

attention_map.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms dates and venues with you.
attention_map.why: Too early to be asked my guest count. I haven't seen anything that makes me trust them yet.

attention_map.quote: Planned by Wedded Concierge, with one Wedded Advisor from enquiry to the wedding weekend.
attention_map.why: It's set out like a proof strip but it just repeats the line above. No numbers, no press, no names. In my other tabs this spot shows press logos or the planners' faces.

attention_map.quote: Monserrate ... hosts private celebrations; roof works with scaffolding run to the first quarter of 2027.
attention_map.why: This is the most convincing thing near the top. Palaces you can actually book, and they're honest that there's scaffolding. Someone checked the details.

Each region gives the airport code, which helps. But 'Ask your Wedded Advisor' appears five times, once on every card, where I wanted a number. With 120 guests I need to know whether a region can take us. It reads like they don't know.

attention_map.quote: state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra. Nothing may be fixed to the heritage.
attention_map.why: This is the kind of detail a real planner warns you about. I trust it.

attention_map.quote: Of all the Europe wedding destinations we plan, Portugal gives couples five things in one country.
attention_map.why: It's fine, but it's about Portugal, not about them. 'We plan' Europe, but they don't show me a single wedding they've planned.

attention_map.quote: exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill.
attention_map.why: Useful. It shows they read contracts on my behalf. This is the closest the page gets to describing the actual service.

attention_map.quote: Many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the city centre, as a guide
attention_map.why: I asked how far it is from the airport, not from the city centre. There are no times at all for the Algarve, the Douro or Comporta. Our rule is within two hours of an airport, and I still can't check it.

attention_map.quote: The US Embassy in Lisbon does not issue a CNI, because no US authority exists to issue one.
attention_map.why: Very thorough, with each passport covered separately and official sources. Probably the best legal summary in my tabs. But it's information. It doesn't sell the firm.

attention_map.quote: What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things: your guest count, the region, the season, how many nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use.
attention_map.why: No figures at all. Nothing on how Wedded Concierge charges, whether it's a planning fee, a percentage or built into supplier prices, or what currency. Every firm says it depends.

attention_map.quote: There is no set Portugal package. Instead, your Wedded Advisor helps you plan a weekend around your guests, and it can include:
attention_map.why: 'Helps you plan' and 'can include' are exactly the vague scope I'm trying to avoid. Even 'An on-the-day coordinator' is only something it 'can include'. Do they handle design, suppliers, guest transfers, the welcome dinner? End to end or not?

attention_map.quote: Guest website in Wonderland Studio: share the schedule, travel and entry rules in one place. [Start for free]
attention_map.why: A free DIY website tool makes this feel like a consumer wedding site, not a full service planner. Not what I came for.
There's no real wedding anywhere on the page. This is the first thing I look for before I go near a form.

attention_map.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your one contact at Wedded Concierge, instead of one conversation per venue.
attention_map.why: No name, no face, no years of experience. 'Instead of one conversation per venue' makes it sound like a go-between, not a planner who's invested in us. And 'Portugal properties are still being confirmed' sounds unfinished.
No idea when, or who. I'm used to a senior reply within a day. The form is easy enough, but I'm not ready to fill it in.
The legal answers are good. The cost answer dodges again. None of the FAQs ask what they do or what they charge.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip links on a planner's page lower the tone. Feels like a magazine, not a firm I'd hand a six-figure budget to.

questions_answered.question: What exactly does end-to-end include?
questions_answered.evidence: 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend' and the venue contract checks hint at it, but s6 only says a weekend 'can include' items and the advisor 'helps you plan'. No clear list of what they do versus what I do.

questions_answered.question: Why an Australian company for a wedding in Europe?
questions_answered.evidence: The page never says where the firm is based or why it suits non-Australians. The US and UK are named, which avoids an Australia-only feel, but nothing gives me a reason to pick them.

questions_answered.question: How far is it from a major airport?
questions_answered.evidence: Nearest airport codes are on every region card. The only time given is 'Many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the city centre, as a guide'. No airport transfer times for any region.

questions_answered.question: How are fees and supplier costs structured, and in what currency?
questions_answered.evidence: Costs tab and FAQ 4 give no figures and no fee model. The venue box explains how venues charge, but nothing explains how Wedded Concierge charges or in what currency.

questions_answered.question: Can we see weddings you have done here?
questions_answered.evidence: The real weddings section is hidden at launch. No Portugal or Europe weddings shown anywhere.

objections_triggered.objection: Vague scope: can't tell if this is a full service planner or a referral service
objections_triggered.triggered_by: "your Wedded Advisor helps you plan a weekend around your guests, and it can include" and "your one contact at Wedded Concierge, instead of one conversation per venue"

objections_triggered.objection: No proof they've done weddings in Portugal
objections_triggered.triggered_by: No real weddings section, and a proof strip with no numbers or press
"Your Wedded Advisor talks you through the options for your plans."

objections_triggered.objection: Nothing feels senior: no named planner, no reply time
Travel time for guests can't be checked
objections_triggered.triggered_by: "Nearest airport: Faro (FAO)" with no transfer time; "15 to 30 minutes from the city centre"

objections_triggered.objection: Why use a firm based in Australia?
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Never addressed; Australian passport and Smartraveller are listed first in the passport sections

trust_signals_noticed: Detailed, sourced legal steps for US and UK passports, 'Checked October 2026'
Honest caveats: Monserrate scaffolding, state events can cancel palace bookings
Venue contract checks (rooms, buy-outs, minimums, VAT)
US and UK named in the brand sentence, not Australia only
turn_offs_noticed: No senior planner names or faces
'Start for free' DIY tool alongside a full service offer

emotional_response.overall: Respect for the research, but cold. It reads like an excellent guide to marrying in Portugal written by a firm that doesn't want to show itself.
emotional_response.emotional_investment: I don't feel anyone here is invested in us. There are no people, no stories, no weddings.

payload.decision_reason: I'd only enquire if scope, proof and fees were clear and the firm felt senior, and this page gives me none of those. I can't see one wedding they've done, I don't know who the advisor is or how quickly they reply, 'can include' leaves the scope open, and there's nothing on how they charge or in what currency. I might copy the legal tab for reference, but the firms in my other tabs show their planners and their weddings, so I'd enquire there.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Honestly, the paperwork section is better than anyone else's. But I'm hiring a planner, not reading a guidebook. Who's our planner? What have they done in Portugal? What do they charge? 'Your Wedded Advisor helps you plan... it can include' could mean anything. And Ronaldo's wedding at the bottom? I'll close this tab.

results.check: Read only persona, artefact and payload schema
Fallback lines used where sign-off pending; hidden sections treated as not visible

assumptions: Read as a US or UK couple with 40 to 150 guests, comparing three or more firms on desktop
The persona's currency preference and service expectations are file assumptions, held lightly
